  factual / structural / scope).

  Pay attention to:

  (1) Universe rule honesty — does source_defined + the table_title +
      db_analog + temporal_note coherently describe the "top-20 man-made
      completed by structural height" universe? Or is the natural-dam
      exclusion under-disclosed?

  (2) Man-made vs natural-origin scoping — verify that Usoi (567 m
      landslide, Tajikistan), The Barrier (500 m lava, Canada), and Lake
      Waikaremoana (250 m landslide, NZ) are the only natural-origin
      entries in the master article's top-N (i.e., we haven't missed
      excluding any other natural dam that would belong in the staged top
      by master rank).

  (3) Source verification — for each of the 20 staged rows, confirm the
      per-dam Wikipedia article + master table support Height, Country,
      River, Year Completed. Per the cycle-2 bridges canonical-source rule
      carried forward: per-dam article wins for Height/Year when per-dam
      infobox + lead concur and master is unsupported.

  (4) Gilgel Gibe III Height discrepancy (the Pingnan-Third-style
      exception) — verify per-dam article infobox + lead both report
      250 m and master-table reports 243 m. Verify the staged value 250 m
      follows the canonical-source rule.

  (5) Year Completed canonical-source applications (4 rows):
      - Jinping-I 2014 (not master 2013)
      - Yusufeli 2022 (not master 2021)
      - Grande Dixence 1961 (not master 1964; per-dam article-lead vs
        commissioning year)
      - Baihetan 2021 (opening-ceremony framing per per-dam article lead)
      Verify each follows the per-dam article lead.

  (6) Vajont Dam "Disused" status — verify staged Year Completed 1959
      (structural completion year per article lead) is defensible despite
      the dam being non-operational post-1963 disaster.

  (7) Sort order: Height DESC primary, Dam ASC alphabetical secondary.
      At Height=250 there's a 3-way tie (Gilgel Gibe III, Laxiwa,
      Mauvoisin) — verify alphabetical G<L<M ordering. At Height=243
      there's a 2-way tie (Alberto Lleras, Mica) — verify A<M.

  (8) Dam name normalization: 'Chicoasén Dam' with acute é per article
      title, 'Jinping-I Dam' with hyphen-Roman-numeral, 'Gilgel Gibe III
      Dam' with III qualifier, 'Sayano-Shushenskaya Dam' with hyphen,
      'Alberto Lleras Dam' (not redirect 'Guavio Dam').

  (9) Entity-class classification: per the locked
      instance_selection_priorities.md inventory, this instance is
      `engineered-structures/dams` (NEW fine-class). After Ready,
      inventory + controlled vocab + rollup will need updating — that's
      a follow-up md task, NOT part of this audit.

  Return condensed verdict block. Append findings to

Verdict: Not ready. Counts by severity: 1 BLOCKING, 2 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. Counts by issue type: factual 1, structural 2, scope-related 0.

Findings:

1. (factual, BLOCKING) Mica Dam's staged Height = 243 m is not supported by the cited per-dam Wikipedia article under the declared per-dam-value source plan. The master list row supports 243 m for Mica Dam (List of tallest dams, Existing table: Mica Dam, 243 m, Canada, Columbia River, 1973; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tallest_dams). But the cited Mica Dam article does not support 243 m: its infobox states Height = 240 m and its history text says the dam was built to 244 m above bedrock (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mica_Dam, infobox Dam and spillways / History). This contradicts the curation record's rule that per-dam articles supply per-row Height values and that height values match between master and per-dam article except Gilgel Gibe III. Minimal fix: either (a) keep 243 m as a master-list-only value and document Mica as a second explicit source-conflict exception where master-list ranking/value wins because the per-dam article is internally inconsistent, or (b) change the CSV height to the chosen per-dam value and reassess sort/universe tie handling around 240 m. The repair must update temporal_note, source_coverage_notes, decision_log, normalization_decisions, and open_questions so the canonical-source rule handles Mica explicitly.

2. (structural, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE) Current-state narrative still has stale China/country-count prose. The CSV country distribution is China 7, Switzerland 2, Turkey 2, and nine singleton countries = 12 distinct countries. collection_summary and draft._extraction_notes mostly state this correctly, but curation.json::decision_log still says China 8 / 40% and says "9 distinct countries" while listing 12 countries. Local evidence: worlds_tallest_dams_by_structural_height.csv has seven China rows; decision_log Rule 6 carries the stale count. Minimal fix: scrub decision_log pre-gate risk (b) and Rule 6 to China 7, 35%, 12 distinct countries.

3. (structural, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE) Current-state narrative undercounts 0.5-m precision rows. The CSV has four decimal-height rows: Xiluodu 285.5, Enguri 271.5, Nuozhadu 261.5, and Tehri 260.5. curation.json::decision_log Rule 5 and normalization_decisions say "Three rows use 0.5 m precision" while naming all four. Minimal fix: change "Three rows" to "Four rows" in both active narrative locations.

Checks that passed:

- Universe rule honesty: table_title, db_analog, temporal_note, collection_summary, source_coverage_notes, decision_log, and proposed_supplements all disclose the man-made/completed filter. source_defined is acceptable because the staged universe is the source-defined master-table top-K with an explicit man-made filter, not curator-selected rows.
- Natural-origin scoping: the master List of tallest dams lead distinguishes natural and man-made dams and the Existing table shows the top natural-origin entries in scope for displacement as Usoi Dam (Landslide, 567 m), The Barrier (Lava, 500 m), and Lake Waikaremoana Dam (Landslide, 250 m). No other natural-origin entry appears above the staged cutoff in the master Existing table.
- Gilgel Gibe III: master list reports 243 m; per-dam article infobox and lead both report 250 m on the Omo River in Ethiopia. The staged 250 m value follows the declared bridges-derived per-dam canonical-source rule.
- Year Completed spot checks: Jinping-I 2014 is supported by its per-dam lead completion sentence despite master 2013; Yusufeli 2022 is supported by per-dam opening/operational framing despite master 2021; Grande Dixence 1961 is supported by per-dam opening/completion framing despite master 1964; Baihetan 2021 is supported by master 2021 and the per-dam opening-date / opening-ceremony framing, while the article also documents full power-station completion in 2022.
- Vajont: Year Completed 1959 is defensible as structural completion/list-year despite disused status after the 1963 disaster; per-dam article and master support the dam as a completed structure.
- CSV integrity: 20 rows, 5 columns, Dam PK unique, source_count = 21 = len(source_urls), sort order Height DESC then Dam ASC passes. Tie ordering passes: 250 m = Gilgel Gibe III, Laxiwa, Mauvoisin; 243 m = Alberto Lleras, Mica.
- Name normalization spot checks pass: Chicoasén acute, Jinping-I hyphen/Roman numeral, Gilgel Gibe III qualifier, Sayano-Shushenskaya hyphen, Alberto Lleras article-title form over Guavio redirect.
- Wiki-family discovery: the cited List of tallest dams is the direct Wikipedia universe/ranking source. Sibling pages such as country-specific tallest-dam lists or List of largest dams do not provide a stronger global structural-height universe for this query.

Minimal repair list:

1. Resolve and document the Mica Dam height conflict under the canonical-source rule; adjust CSV only if the curator chooses a per-dam value over the master-list value.
2. Correct decision_log China/country-count prose to China 7 / 35% / 12 distinct countries.
3. Correct the 0.5-m precision prose from three rows to four rows.
